Task: build part 2 of "Screenshot Receipts" in gemini-4-braincells (Shill or Chill). A screenshot of a social-media post is a claim. Given what Nemotron read from the screenshot, find the real post and check whether it matches. Two sibling threads run in parallel: part 1, "Nemotron screenshot reader" (owns media/, branch `feat/nemotron-screenshot-read`), and part 3, "Nemotron as the fast main AI for lookup" (also edits lookup/service.py). The user's goal: lookups should feel instant, with Nemotron as the main AI for speed. Every call you add must be time-budgeted, and independent calls must run in parallel.

Input contract, produced by part 1 in `media/screenshot.py`. Code against exactly this. Stack on part 1's branch once it is pushed. Until then, use a local copy of the dataclass and drop it when you rebase:
```python
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ScreenshotPost:
    media_hash: str
    platform: str            # x | bluesky | threads | facebook | instagram | tiktok | other | unknown
    display_name: str | None
    handle: str | None       # without @
    shown_time: str | None   # verbatim, e.g. "3:14 PM · Nov 13, 2026" or "2h"
    text: str | None
    counts: dict[str, int | None]   # replies, reposts, quotes, likes, views, bookmarks; None = not shown
    ui_oddities: list[str]
    confidence: float
    model: str
    latency_ms: int
```

Scope:
1. New `lookup/receipts.py`: `find_original(shot, deps, budget) -> ScreenshotReceipt`.
   - Bluesky: resolve the handle to a DID (lookup/bsky.py), then search that author's posts for the phrase with `searchPosts` and `from:`, falling back to the author feed.
   - X: Oxylabs `/search` with `site:x.com/<handle>` plus the exact phrase, then read the candidate post with the existing xpage parser and get its exact time from the snowflake id.
   - Compare with lookup/textsim.py, and compare shown_time with the real time. Relative times ("2h") get an uncertainty window, like `Page.time_uncertainty_s`.
   - Labels: `matches` (real post link), `differs` (real post link plus a word-level diff), `not_found` (wording: "no matching post found: it may be deleted, private or never posted", never "fake").
   - Counts are context only, never a verdict, because posts gain and lose likes.
   - Every fetch becomes a Receipt, the same as the rest of lookup.
2. Lookup integration: a new `screenshot` step after `media` (update the step list in lookup/README.md and models.py). Run it for each submitted-post image that Nemotron marked as a screenshot of a post. Add the receipt to `LookupResult` (new field plus README JSON docs) with an `Edge` rel such as `screenshot_of`. Gemini/assessment may cite it. Keep the wiring in service.py small (a call into receipts.py), because part 3 is refactoring service.py for speed. Rebase onto whichever lands first.
3. Media worker: after part 1 merges, rows that have `detail.screenshot` get an extra evidence row `detail.type='screenshot_receipt'`, upserted on the stable (cluster, media hash) key like ocr_template rows, so the Gemini analyst and the dashboard see it. Add a dashboard card showing the screenshot and the real post side by side, with the diff (web/public/index.html, one file, no build).
4. Tests with recorded fixtures (no live calls), covering: Bluesky match, X match with snowflake time, text differs, not found, relative time, missing handle (skip with a reason).

Honesty rules from lookup/README.md apply. Never guess values (unknown = null). The label describes the screenshot, never a person.

Working style: use multiple subagents in parallel. For example: one each for the Bluesky resolver, the X resolver, compare+labels, lookup wiring, tests, and dashboard. Then do Sol review rounds: Codex gpt-6.1-sol, reasoning high, via delegate_task, a new delegate each round, until it says approved. Fix the findings yourself. Start with `entire brain brief` + `entire graph query` per .entire/agent-guide.md.

Git: pushes from worktrees of the shared /srv checkout can fail on other users' mode-600 Entire objects. If that happens, clone https://github.com/JustinasLa/gemini-4-braincells.git into ~/work/<name>, fetch your branch into it and push from there. Open a PR once Sol approves. Do NOT merge or deploy: report back with the PR URL and an example lookup result.

# lookup/: trace one link through X, Bluesky and the web

A user pastes a link (an X post, a Bluesky post, a profile or any web page). The lookup collects
real, live data about it and returns it with a receipt for every fact:

- **The post itself** (Oxylabs `/scrape` of the X page; Bluesky public AppView): author, text,
  exact creation time, the counts X shows (views, replies, reposts, likes, bookmarks), the
  linked card and the media.
- **The author's history** (Oxylabs `/scrape` of the profile): join date, followers, following,
  post count, bio, and the recent posts the profile page shows, with their exact times.
- **Where the text appears** (Oxylabs `/search`, exact phrase, the open web plus `site:x.com`
  and `site:bsky.app`; Bluesky `searchPosts`): copies and quotes from other accounts, each with
  its own time. X post ids are snowflakes, so every X hit gets its creation time from the id
  alone (`(id >> 22) + 1288834974657` ms), no extra request.
- **The linked page and the coverage** (Oxylabs `/scrape` with AI extraction; `/search` for the
  headline / claim): publisher, date, headline, main claims; other outlets on the same story.
- **Media** (Nemotron 3.5 Super VL): description and OCR of the post's images; the OCR text is
  searched like the post text, so a screenshot that is passed around is found too.
- **Our monitor**: whether the link, text or accounts are in a cluster the detector watches
  (`api/store.py`), and that cluster's detector status.
- **Gemini** writes a short, cited reading of the collected receipts: origin, corroboration,
  spread pattern, counter-evidence, what would change the reading. It may cite only receipt ids
  that exist (checked in code). It never sets the status.

**Status rule (honesty):** `status` is `matched` only when the input hits a cluster we monitor;
the coordination verdict is then that cluster's detector status. Otherwise `status` is
`insufficient`: one link's web footprint is not proof of coordination, and the copy pattern is
shown as data (counts, times, accounts), never as a verdict. Search results are a sample, not a
census: the notes say so.

## API

```
POST /api/lookup        {"url": "https://x.com/user/status/123"}   or {"text": "..."}
  -> 202 LookupResult (state "running"); repeated input within LOOKUP_CACHE_TTL_S -> cached result
GET  /api/lookup/{id}   -> LookupResult; poll every ~1.5 s until state is "done" or "failed"
```

Errors: 400 bad input, 429 rate limit (`LOOKUP_MAX_PER_HOUR` overall, `LOOKUP_MAX_PER_IP_PER_HOUR`
per client), 503 when Oxylabs isn't configured, 404 unknown/expired id.
Jobs live in the API process (single uvicorn worker) for `LOOKUP_JOB_TTL_S`.

## LookupResult (JSON)

All arrays grow while `state` is `running`; the client re-renders on each poll. Times are ISO
8601 UTC. Unknown values are `null`, never guessed.

`copies_bsky`, `coverage`, `media`, `verify`, `monitor`, `assess`. Steps that don't apply are
`skipped`. Order of work: post + author; then the searches, linked page and media in parallel;
then `verify` (candidates from every search); then `monitor` (with every link, text and account
found); then Gemini. Every provider call checks the time budget first (the last 25 s are kept
for Gemini); a step that runs out says "time budget used up".

## Rules that keep it honest (and why)

- **Times.** X post times come from the post id (snowflake), so every X post found, even one
  only seen in a search result, has its exact creation time. Bluesky times are the record's
  `createdAt`. Web pages get the publisher's date when the scrape extracts one, otherwise the
  search engine's hint ("3 hours ago" relative to the search) marked `search_hint`.
- **Counts.** X hides zero counts on the logged-out page, and the reposts / likes / bookmarks
  numbers carry no label, so they are assigned only when all of them are shown; otherwise they
  are `null` (never guessed, never 0). Replies and the post's views are labelled and kept.
  Counts are what the page showed at `metrics_as_of`.
- **Copies are verified.** A search hit only says the text appears there. Up to
  `LOOKUP_VERIFY_MAX` candidate X posts are read on their own page: a quote of the post, a
  reply to it, or a copy of its words (similarity = share of the post's words the copy
  carries). On 13 Nov 2026 the top "copy" hit for a viral joke was in fact a quote post.
  X hits sharing under 35% of the words are dropped (search engines match loose keywords).
- **Images.** Nemotron reads the post's own images; their text (8+ words) is searched like the
  post text. Link-card thumbnails are described but not searched (their text is a photo label).
  A post that is only an image is searched by the text inside it.
- **Short links** (t.co etc.) are resolved before the page is scraped.
- **Origin needs a clear lead.** A page is the origin only if the latest time its date allows
  (a day for a date-only hint, the unit for "3 hours ago") is before every post. Only posts read
  on their own page or API count as copies, in the spread and for the origin.
- **No verdict from a footprint.** `status` is `matched` only when a monitored cluster shared
  the link or the text. A cluster that only contains an account seen in the lookup is listed as
  context (`verdict_applies: false`), never as this link's verdict. Gemini's `llm_reading` is shown as its
  reading, never as the status, and keeps only citations of receipts that exist.

curl -s -XPOST localhost:8005/api/lookup -H 'content-type: application/json' \

from __future__ import annotations

import re

_URL = re.compile(r"https?://\S+")
_TOKEN = re.compile(r"[\w']+", re.UNICODE)
_QUOTES = str.maketrans({"’": "'", "‘": "'", "“": '"', "”": '"', "—": " ", "–": " "})
_LEADING_DATE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(?:\d+\s+(?:second|minute|hour|day|week|month|year)s?\s+ago|"
    r"[A-Z][a-z]{2,8}\.? \d{1,2}, \d{4})\s*[·—–\-]\s*"
)
STOP = frozenset("a an the and or of to in on at is it that this for with as by be are was".split())


def tokens(text: str | None) -> list[str]:
    if not text:
        return []
    t = _URL.sub(" ", text.translate(_QUOTES).lower())
    return [w for w in _TOKEN.findall(t) if w not in STOP]


def strip_snippet(snippet: str) -> str:
    """Drop the '23 hours ago · ' / 'Nov 13, 2026 — ' prefix and a trailing ellipsis."""
    s = _LEADING_DATE.sub("", snippet or "").strip()
    return re.sub(r"\s*(?:\.\.\.|…)\s*$", "", s)


def similarity(candidate: str | None, reference: str | None, *, truncated: bool = False) -> float:
    """0..1: how much of the reference text the candidate carries.

    `truncated` (a search snippet): share of the candidate's words found in the reference.
    Otherwise the larger of the Jaccard overlap and the share of the reference's words the
    candidate contains (so "Stephen King: <the same text>" still counts as carrying it), the
    latter only when the reference has 6+ distinct words (short texts match too easily)."""
    a, b = set(tokens(candidate)), set(tokens(reference))
    if not a or not b:
        return 0.0
    if truncated:
        return len(a & b) / len(a)
    jac = len(a & b) / len(a | b)
    if len(b) < 6:
        return jac
    return max(jac, 0.95 * len(a & b) / len(b))


def phrase(text: str | None, n_words: int = 12) -> str | None:
    """An exact-search phrase: the first `n_words` words of the text, without URLs or mentions.
    None when the text is too short (< 5 words) to search for reliably."""
    if not text:
        return None
    t = _URL.sub(" ", text.translate(_QUOTES))
    words = [w for w in t.split() if not w.startswith("@") and not w.startswith("#")]
    if len(words) < 5:
        return None
    out = " ".join(words[:n_words])
    return out.replace('"', "").strip(" .,:;")

def snippet_time(snippet: str, at: datetime) -> tuple[datetime | None, float | None]:
    """A search engine's date hint and how uncertain it is (seconds after `time`).

    '23 hours ago' -> (at - 23 h, 3600): the engine rounds to the unit. 'Nov 13, 2026 — ...'
    -> (that midnight UTC, 86400): any time that day."""
    if m := _REL_AGO.match(snippet or ""):
        unit = _REL_UNIT[m.group(2).lower()]
        return at - timedelta(seconds=(int(m.group(1)) + 1) * unit), 2 * unit
    from sources.oxylabs import leading_date

    d = leading_date(snippet or "")

def _page_time(published_at: str | None) -> tuple[datetime | None, float | None]:
    """The publisher's date as extracted, and its uncertainty (seconds after `time`)."""
    if not published_at:
        return None, None
    raw = published_at.strip()
    try:
        t = datetime.fromisoformat(raw.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    except ValueError:
        return None, None
    if len(raw) <= 10:  # a date only: any time that day
        return t.replace(tzinfo=UTC), 86400.0
    if t.tzinfo is None:  # a clock time in an unknown zone: within about 14 h of UTC
        return t.replace(tzinfo=UTC) - timedelta(hours=14), 28 * 3600.0
    return t, 0.0


def _x_title(title: str) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
    """'Name on X: "text..."' -> (name, text); 'Name on X' -> (name, None)."""
    m = re.match(r'^(.*?) on X(?:: "(.*?)(?:"(?: / X)?)?)?\s*$', title or "", re.S)
    if not m:
        return None, None
    text = (m.group(2) or "").strip().removesuffix("...").removesuffix("…").strip() or None

                found.append(bp.id)
            st.found = found
            st.detail = f"{len(found)} Bluesky posts with the same text"

    def _coverage(self) -> None:
        q = self._card_title or textsim.phrase(self._subject_text, 14)
        if not q:
            self.skip("coverage", "nothing to search for")
            return
        with self.step("coverage") as st:
            q = q.replace('"', "")
            hits, call = self._search(q, 10)
            at = _now()
            rid = self.receipt(
                "oxylabs", "/search", f"Coverage search: {len(hits)} results", query=q, call=call
            )
            ref = self._subject_text or q
            found = []
            for h in hits:
                if X_STATUS_RE.match(h.url) or "x.com/" in h.url or "twitter.com/" in h.url:
                    continue
                if (nid := self._classify_hit(h, rid, at, reference=ref)) and nid.startswith(
                    "page:"
                ):
                    found.append(nid)
            st.found = found
            st.detail = f"{len(found)} pages on the story"

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- media (Nemotron)
    def _media(self, ocr_as_text: bool = False) -> None:
        urls = self._media_urls[: self.deps.media_max]
        if not urls:
            self.skip("media", "the post has no images")
            return
        if not self.deps.nemotron:
            self.skip("media", "Nemotron is not configured on this server")
            return
        with self.step("media") as st:
            from media.nemotron import MediaInput, is_vl_model

            http = self.deps.http or httpx.Client(timeout=20, follow_redirects=False)
            texts, read = [], 0
            for url in urls:
                if domain(url) not in MEDIA_HOSTS or not url.startswith("https://"):
                    continue  # only the platforms' own image CDNs are downloaded
                own_media = "/card_img/" not in url  # link-card thumbnails: describe only
                data, mime = _download_image(http, url)
                if data is None:
                    continue
                h = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
                self._spend(45)  # one bounded Nemotron attempt
                started = time.monotonic()
                a = self.deps.nemotron.analyze(
                    MediaInput(media_hash=f"lookup:{h}", mime_type=mime, data=data, url=url),
                    context=self._subject_text,
                )
                if not is_vl_model(a.model):
                    self.note(
                        f"Media reading skipped: the endpoint answered as {a.model}, "
                        "not a vision-language model."
                    )
                    continue
                rid = self.receipt(
                    "nemotron",
                    "chat.completions",
                    f"Nemotron read the image: {a.description[:200]}",
                    source_url=url,
                    latency_ms=a.latency_ms or int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000),
                )
                with self.lock:
                    self.result.media.append(
                        MediaFinding(
                            media_url=url,
                            post_id=self.result.subject_id,
                            description=a.description,
                            extracted_text=a.extracted_text,
                            reuse_cues=a.reuse_cues,
                            manipulation_cues=a.manipulation_cues,
                            confidence=a.confidence,
                            model=a.model,
                            latency_ms=a.latency_ms,
                            receipt_id=rid,
                        )
                    )
                read += 1
                if own_media:
                    texts.extend(a.extracted_text)
            found = []
            # the longest line first: headers ("NETWORK & OPERATIONS", dates) make poor queries
            texts = sorted(texts, key=lambda t: -len(t.split()))
            ocr = textsim.phrase(" ".join(texts), 10)
            if len(textsim.tokens(" ".join(texts))) < OCR_MIN_WORDS:
                ocr = None
            if ocr and ocr_as_text:
                # the post is the image: its text is what the copy searches look for
                self._subject_text = " ".join(texts)
                self.note(
                    "The post has no text of its own; the searches use the text Nemotron "
                    "read inside its image."
                )
                ocr = None
            if ocr and textsim.similarity(ocr, self._subject_text, truncated=True) < VERBATIM:
                # the image's own text, searched like the post text: where does it circulate?
                q = f'"{ocr}"'
                hits, call = self._search(q, 10)
                at = _now()
                rid = self.receipt(
                    "oxylabs",
                    "/search",
                    f"Search for the text inside the image (Nemotron OCR): {len(hits)} results",
                    query=q,
                    call=call,
                )
                for hit in hits:
                    ref = " ".join(texts)
                    if nid := self._classify_hit(hit, rid, at, reference=ref, min_sim=COPY_MIN):
                        found.append(nid)
                        if self.result.subject_id and nid.startswith("x:"):
                            self.add_edge(
                                nid,
                                self.result.subject_id,
                                "media",
                                tool="nemotron",
                                note="same text inside the image",
                            )
            st.found = found
            st.detail = f"{read} image(s) read" + (
                f" · OCR text found in {len(found)} places"
                if ocr
                else " · its text drives the searches"
                if ocr_as_text and texts
                else ""
            )

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- monitor
    def _monitor(self) -> None:
        if not self.deps.store:
            self.skip("monitor", "database not configured")
            return

"""Screenshot receipts: a screenshot of a post is a claim. Find the real post and check it.

Input: what Nemotron read from the screenshot (`media.screenshot.ScreenshotPost`). Output: a
`ScreenshotReceipt` (lookup/models.py) labelled

- `matches`   the real post was found and says what the screenshot shows (link to it);
- `differs`   the real post was found but its words (or its time) differ (link + word diff);
- `not_found` no matching post found: it may be deleted, private or never posted;
- `unchecked` the screenshot can't be checked (no legible handle, platform we can't read,
              time budget used up), with the reason.

The label describes the screenshot, never a person. Counts are context only (posts gain and
lose likes); they never decide the label. Every fetch becomes a Receipt via `deps.receipt`,
the same as the rest of lookup. Independent calls run in parallel, each clamped to `budget`.

Resolvers: Bluesky in lookup/receipts_bsky.py, X in lookup/receipts_x.py.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import time
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from typing import Any, Protocol

from lookup.models import DiffPart, Metrics, ScreenshotReceipt

try:  # part 1 (feat/nemotron-screenshot-read) owns the contract
    from media.screenshot import ScreenshotPost
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - local copy until part 1 lands; drop on rebase

    @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
    class ScreenshotPost:  # type: ignore[no-redef]
        media_hash: str
        platform: str  # x | bluesky | threads | facebook | instagram | tiktok | other | unknown
        display_name: str | None
        handle: str | None  # without @
        shown_time: str | None  # verbatim, e.g. "3:14 PM · Nov 13, 2026" or "2h"
        text: str | None
        counts: dict[str, int | None]  # replies, reposts, quotes, likes, views, bookmarks
        ui_oddities: list[str]
        confidence: float
        model: str
        latency_ms: int


log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

NOT_FOUND = "no matching post found: it may be deleted, private or never posted"
COUNTS_NOTE = "Counts change as people like and repost; shown as context, never as a verdict."
SUPPORTED = ("x", "bluesky")


class ShotTimeUp(RuntimeError):
    """The time budget ran out before a call could start."""


class ReceiptSink(Protocol):
    """Same signature as `lookup.service.Lookup.receipt`; returns the new receipt id."""

    def __call__(
        self,
        tool: str,
        endpoint: str,
        summary: str,
        *,
        source_url: str | None = None,
        query: str | None = None,
        call: dict | None = None,
        ok: bool = True,
        latency_ms: int | None = None,
    ) -> int: ...


@dataclass
class Budget:
    """An absolute end (time.monotonic()) for every call this check makes."""

    deadline: float

    @classmethod
    def seconds(cls, s: float) -> Budget:
        return cls(time.monotonic() + s)

    def left(self) -> float:
        return self.deadline - time.monotonic()

    def check(self, need_s: float = 3.0) -> None:
        """Gate before every provider call: raise ShotTimeUp when `need_s` no longer fits."""
        if self.left() < need_s:
            raise ShotTimeUp("time budget used up")


@dataclass
class ReceiptDeps:
    receipt: ReceiptSink
    oxylabs: Any = None  # sources.oxylabs.OxylabsClient (search, scrape_markdown); thread-safe
    bsky: Any = None  # lookup.bsky.BlueskyClient
    # the latest moment the screenshot can have been taken: the time the post carrying it was
    # created, else the check's own time. Relative times ("2h") count back from it.
    anchor: datetime | None = None
    now: Callable[[], datetime] = field(default=lambda: datetime.now(UTC))
    workers: int = 4  # parallel calls per check (a private pool: never the caller's pool)
    x_read_max: int = 2  # X candidate posts read on their own page


@dataclass
class Candidate:
    """A real post that may be the one in the screenshot, read on its own page or API."""

    id: str  # "x:<status id>" or the at:// uri, as lookup Post ids
    platform: str  # x | bluesky
    url: str
    handle: str | None
    author_name: str | None
    text: str
    created_at: datetime | None
    time_source: str | None  # snowflake | api
    metrics: Metrics | None
    receipt_id: int | None
    source: str = ""  # how it was found: searchPosts | author_feed | /search | profile ...


def find_original(shot: ScreenshotPost, deps: ReceiptDeps, budget: Budget) -> ScreenshotReceipt:
    """Find the real post the screenshot shows and compare. Never raises: a failure or an
    exhausted budget becomes an `unchecked` receipt with the reason."""
    raise NotImplementedError


def judge(
    shot: ScreenshotPost,
    candidates: list[Candidate],
    anchor: datetime,
    *,
    receipt_ids: list[int] | None = None,
) -> ScreenshotReceipt:
    """Pure: pick the best candidate, diff the words, check the time, set the label."""
    raise NotImplementedError


def shown_window(
    shown_time: str | None, anchor: datetime
) -> tuple[datetime | None, datetime | None, str | None]:
    """The real times a shown time allows: (earliest, latest, note). None = open on that side.

    Absolute times are in the viewer's unknown time zone (within about 14 h of UTC). Relative
    times ("2h") count back from `anchor`, the latest moment the screenshot can have been
    taken; how long before that it was taken is unknown, so the window is open on the early
    side. Unparseable -> (None, None, note)."""
    raise NotImplementedError


def word_diff(shot_text: str | None, post_text: str | None) -> list[DiffPart]:
    """Word-level diff, ignoring case, quote styles, punctuation and URLs (screenshots
    truncate links). Runs of equal ops are merged."""
    raise NotImplementedError
